claim: XSS occurs when untrusted input reaches an output context and is interpreted as active content (script) rather than inert data.

provenance.title: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

claim: Reflected XSS occurs when the injected script is echoed back in the immediate HTTP response to a request and is not stored on the server.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Stored XSS occurs when the injected payload is persisted (database, file, log) and later served to other users.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: DOM-based XSS occurs entirely client-side: a script reads a source (e.g. location.hash) and writes it to a dangerous sink without the server rendering the payload.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: The correct output encoding is determined by the context the data lands in; HTML-entity encoding that stops HTML-text injection does not stop injection inside a JavaScript string.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: In HTML text context, encoding <, >, &, ", ' to entities prevents breaking out of text into markup.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: In an HTML attribute value, unquoted attributes are dangerous because whitespace or event-handler attributes can be injected without needing a quote character.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: element.innerHTML and outerHTML parse their string as HTML, so assigning untrusted data to them is a DOM XSS sink.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: element.textContent and element.innerText treat their value as text, not markup, so they are safe DOM sinks for untrusted data.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: document.write and document.writeln parse their argument as HTML and are DOM XSS sinks.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: eval, Function, setTimeout/setInterval with a string argument, and similar APIs execute their string as JavaScript and are code-execution sinks.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Setting an anchor's href or an iframe's src to a javascript: URL executes script when activated; URL-scheme allow-listing (http/https only) prevents this.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: location.hash, location.search, document.referrer, window.name and postMessage data are attacker-controllable DOM sources.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Mutation XSS (mXSS) arises when the browser's HTML parser re-serializes and re-parses markup so that a payload considered safe by a sanitizer becomes active after mutation.

provenance.title: XSS Filter Evasion Cheat Sheet

claim: A robust defense against DOM sinks that require HTML is to sanitize with a well-maintained library (e.g. DOMPurify) configured for the target context, rather than hand-rolled regexes.

provenance.title: DOMPurify README

claim: Blocklist / regex filtering of tags or keywords is unreliable against XSS because of the many equivalent encodings and parser quirks; allow-list and contextual encoding are preferred.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Content Security Policy can mitigate XSS impact by restricting script sources; a strict nonce- or hash-based CSP without 'unsafe-inline' blocks injected inline scripts.

provenance.title: Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet

claim: 'unsafe-inline' in a CSP script-src negates most of CSP's XSS protection because it re-permits inline scripts and event handlers.

provenance.title: Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet

claim: Trusted Types (require-trusted-types-for 'script') forces DOM injection sinks to receive a typed, policy-vetted value, eliminating most DOM XSS sink misuse.

provenance.title: Trusted Types

claim: React escapes string children by default, so {userInput} rendered as text is safe; the danger is dangerouslySetInnerHTML, which bypasses that escaping.

provenance.title: React docs: dangerouslySetInnerHTML

claim: Angular sanitizes interpolated and bound values by default; bypassSecurityTrustHtml and similar APIs disable that protection and reintroduce XSS risk.

provenance.title: Angular security guide

claim: Vue's v-html directive renders raw HTML and bypasses Vue's default text escaping, so it is a template XSS sink for untrusted data.

provenance.title: Vue security guide

claim: In a JavaScript string literal context, HTML-entity encoding is ineffective; the value must be JavaScript-string escaped (\xHH / \uHHHH) or, better, passed as data via JSON.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Reflecting untrusted data inside a <script> block is dangerous even when HTML-encoded, because the HTML parser does not decode entities inside script content.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: For URL context, values placed into a query string or path must be URL-encoded, and the scheme must be validated to prevent javascript:/data: execution.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Server-side reflection of a request parameter into HTML without encoding is the canonical reflected XSS root cause.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: encodeURIComponent protects data placed in a URL query value but does NOT make it safe to place in HTML or JavaScript contexts.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: setAttribute for a non-event, non-URL attribute (e.g. class, title) treats the value as text and does not execute script, unlike setting on* handler attributes.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Assigning to an element's on* event-handler property or attribute with untrusted data is a code-execution sink.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: insertAdjacentHTML parses HTML like innerHTML and is a DOM XSS sink; insertAdjacentText is the safe counterpart.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: jQuery's $(html) / .html() / .append(html) parse and insert HTML, making them DOM XSS sinks when passed untrusted strings.

provenance.title: jQuery API: jQuery( html )

claim: A correct fix generally combines contextual output encoding at the sink with input validation as defense in depth, not input validation alone.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: template literals or DOM text APIs that never parse HTML are structurally safe; the safest remediation removes the HTML-parsing sink rather than trying to clean the input.

provenance.title: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Double-encoding and mixed-context reflection (data flowing through two contexts, e.g. HTML attribute then JavaScript) require encoding for the innermost executing context.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: A value that is HTML-encoded then inserted with textContent is doubly safe but may display literal entities; encoding must match the sink to be both safe and correct.

provenance.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

claim: Specific published CVE advisories for XSS in named product versions are volatile facts that should be retrieved, not memorized into model weights.
